prompt: An alcohol with M⁺ = 74 shows a prominent peak at m/z = 56 (loss of 18). What's the fragmentation pathway?

options.label: Loss of H₂O (18 Da) via E1-type cleavage from M⁺• — gives alkene radical cation
Loss of NH₃ (17 Da) — the mass-18 peak is actually the M+1 isotope peak
Loss of two methyl radicals (2 × 15 = 30), with a rearrangement giving net 18
Loss of CO (28 Da), with concurrent H₂ gain, giving net -18

concepts: alcohol loss of water in MS
explanation: Alcohols readily lose H₂O (18 Da) in MS via E1-type cleavage from M⁺•, giving an alkene radical cation. M-18 is a HALLMARK peak of alcohols. If α-cleavage also happens, you see M-alkyl peaks too. The simple arithmetic (74 - 18 = 56) and alcohol character make loss of water the obvious call.
